facts.material: acrylic (poly(methyl methacrylate)) panels; polycarbonate panels (separate articles or layers, proportions not stated)
facts.form: flat rigid panels/sheets, presumed noncellular, not reinforced and not combined with non-plastic materials, not further worked beyond cutting to rectangular shape

gri_path: First-named article classified: acrylic panels (polycarbonate panels classify separately)

GRI 1: heading 3920 covers other plates and sheets of plastics, noncellular and not reinforced or combined; rectangular panels only cut to size stay in 3920 (chapter 39 note 10); heading 3925 builders' ware (chapter 39 note 11) does not list plain wall panels
GRI 6: 3920.51 of poly(methyl methacrylate); 3920.51.50 other (not flexible); suffix .90 other (no flame retardant stated)

rejected_alternatives.reason: polycarbonate sheets; applies to the polycarbonate panels (classify separately), or to a laminated panel in which polycarbonate predominates by weight
applies if the panels are laminated with or embed non-plastic decorative materials (fabric, natural materials); not stated
builders' ware is limited by chapter 39 note 11; plain decorative sheets are not listed
only if the panels are worked beyond rectangular cutting (drilled, shaped, edged)
requires non-flexible sheets containing flame retardant; none stated

missing_facts: Are the panels a single laminate of acrylic and polycarbonate? If so, which polymer predominates by weight?
Do the panels contain embedded decorative non-plastic interlayers, or are they worked beyond rectangular cutting?
Do the acrylic sheets contain a flame retardant?
classification.rationale: Decorative acrylic panels used for wall paneling and furniture are rigid PMMA sheets, which heading 3920 covers as noncellular, unreinforced plastic sheets. They fall in 3920.51.50 as non-flexible PMMA and in suffix .90 absent a flame retardant. NY L80956 (in force) classified acrylic (PMMA) sheets used to make other products in 3920.51.5000. The polycarbonate panels would go separately to 3920.61; lamination or embedded decorative materials would change the heading.
